units.translation: χλούνην [the wild boar] some say is foaming; for χλουδεῖν [to foam] some Dorians used to say; others say it means a rogue; for one of the ancient iambic poets said: “ἀνὴρ ὅδ᾽ ἐσπέρης καθεύδοντα | ἄπουν ἔδησε χλούνην” [this man at evening bound a sleeping footless wild boar] (χλούνην [wild boar] from which he stripped
a kind of locusts) said that χλούνην [wild boar] is, just as also in Aeschylus in the Edonians
μακροσκελὴς μὲν ἄρα ρα μὴ χλούνης [long-legged indeed, surely not a wild boar]

that χλούνης [wild boar] also signifies a castrated animal, not only Aeschylus provides usage, but also Aelian especially in his works on providence, calling χλούνην [wild boar] the castrated one; and Aristotle according to the geographer calls χλούνην σῦν [wild boar] the castrated pig
ΑΓΓ. μακροσκελὴς μέν. ΛΥΚ. ἆρα μὴ χλούνης τις ἦν [MESSENGER: Long-legged indeed. LYCUS: Surely he was not some wild boar?]
μάντις τοι τὰν νύκτα χροΐζεται ὁ καλαμαία [the mantis, the locust, will touch your skin at night]

Perhaps then Theocritus, wishing to say the thin and wasted one, says this. Or the one that sees something harmful and difficult. For Aristarchus in his commentary on the Lycurgus of Aeschylus says that this locust, if it looks at any animal, becomes an evil to that one. It is green and has very long and slender legs, and moves them constantly

ἢ ή σὴ ἐρωμένη η ἐοικυῖα τῇ καλαμαίᾳ ὀνομαζομένη, τῇ πρὸς μαντείας ἐπιτηδείᾳ, περιβαλεῖται τὸν χρῶτά σου κατὰ τὴν νύκτα · τουτέστιν, ἡ ἰσχνὴ καὶ λεπτὴ καὶ μακροσκελής συγκοιμηθήσεταί σοι [or your beloved, resembling the so-called locust, the one suitable for divination, will embrace your skin at night; that is, the thin and slender and long-legged one will sleep with you]
γένος τι ἀκρίδων [a kind of locusts]

The word χλοῦνις [green crop], not read elsewhere, is mentioned by Arcadius p. 32, 18 among nouns ending in -vic together with βοῦνις [hill]. The scholiast confused it with χλούνης [wild boar], taking it in the sense in which Aristotle, as we just said, used it; he noted: χλούνις [green crop] (thus Robortellus: χλουν, i.e. χλούνης [wild boar] M) is the vigorous cutting, from χλόη [young green shoot] or because χλοῦνις [green crop] is the pig, and boars are constantly castrated, therefore he called the cutting swinish, not human.
and by the destruction of seed (thus Erfurdtius for ἀποφθοραί [destructions]) of children the green crop is damaged.

χλούνης [wild boar] M) is the vigorous cutting, from χλόη [young green shoot] or because χλοῦνις [green crop] is the pig, and boars are constantly castrated, therefore he called the cutting swinish, not human

The primary meaning of the word is green, verdant, in which sense Hermann at Suppl. 63, where in M is read about the nightingale ἅτ᾽ ἀπό χώρων πουταμῶν τ᾽ ἐγρομένα πενθεῖ νέον οἶκτον ἠθέων [which, rising from places and rivers, laments a new pitiful song of youths], conjectured ἅτ᾽ ἀπὸ χλωρῶν πετάλων ἐγρομένα [which, rising from green leaves], not very plausibly, since the following words rather require what I conjectured: ἀπὸ χώρων ποθ' ἑῶν εἰργομένα [excluded from her own places].
they shook their hearts with pale fear.
